CHEAP_DATA_NOW: openFDA enforcement API free; one metadata sample exposes recall initiation, classification and weekly report dates. FDA documents a separate history feature with last-posted/modified dates, but it is not the same as the simple openFDA current record.
CHEAP_EXPRESSION: A fixed public disclosure/classification update mapped to one traded parent, entered strictly after proven availability; never use recall initiation as first-public time.
FAILED_CRITERIA: First public-time clock and PIT classification state; stable parent mapping.
FATAL_PROBLEM: openFDA sample has no first-public timestamp or PIT field history. Prior consignee/public notification may precede weekly report. Subsidiary mapping and precise public clock remain unresolved; a historical date-return join would leak/mis-time news.
LESSON: Initiation, classification, weekly report and actual publication are different clocks. Preserve the newly documented history route without pretending the simple API is PIT.
MECHANISM: Delayed processing of newly public severe product-recall information can reprice a listed issuer once investors recognize revenue/liability consequences.
NEXT_DECISION: Reopen only with a bounded history-endpoint/time qualification. Next L0 public Russell deletion forced flows, with prices unopened.
POWER_LIMITATION: One schema probe, zero issuer outcomes.
UNCERTAINTY: Separate free FDA event/product-history route may support a later conservative/PIT clock; not qualified here.
WHO_PAYS: Investors quoting before incorporating incremental public safety information; affected firm cash flows bear recall costs.
WHY_PERSIST: Fragmented regulator updates, subsidiary/brand mapping and low-salience recalls can slow diffusion, especially in small issuers.

exposure.scope: FDA dates/schema only, no traded-parent selection or return join.
